counterevidence_considered.description: Identical flux values recur within the restored group (17.0 on CLR-02 and CLR-24; 19.0 on CLR-08 and CLR-18), which could superficially suggest a duplicated measurement entering the test twice; however, these rows belong to different collar_id values in different basins, so they are distinct independent units rather than repeated entries of the same unit.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: duplicate flux values across distinct collar_ids

evidence.description: The data description names collar_id as the independent-unit column and states each collar label appears on exactly one row, one collar per hydrologically disconnected basin.
evidence.observed_value: Independent unit column: collar_id; each label appears on exactly one row

source_refs.quoted_text:
- collar_id: unique label of the gas-flux collar, which also identifies the
  basin it sits in (each label appears on exactly one row)

evidence.description: Inspection of all 24 data rows shows 24 distinct collar_id values (CLR-01 through CLR-24) with no duplicates, so each independent unit contributes exactly one row to the test.
evidence.observed_value: 24 rows, 24 unique collar_id values, 12 drained and 12 restored

evidence.description: The workflow enforces one row per independent unit before running the test, raising an error if any collar_id repeats, and passes each group's values once into a single Welch t-test with no duplication, resampling, or row expansion anywhere in the script.
evidence.observed_value: uniqueness guard on collar_id plus a single ttest_ind call on the raw per-collar vectors

evidence.description: Recomputing the group summaries from the raw CSV reproduces the report's values (drained mean 6.00, restored mean 18.00, n = 12 per group), confirming the test consumed exactly the 24 single-entry rows and the reported result matches the workflow output.
evidence.observed_value: drained sum 72.0/12 = 6.00; restored sum 216.0/12 = 18.00; matches report table

source_refs.quoted_text: [selected-result] Rewetted peat collars emitted substantially more methane than drained collars: mean difference 12.00 mg m^-2 h^-1 (95% CI 8.59 to 15.41), Welch t(19.29) = 7.35, p < 0.0001, with 12 collars per group and one flux measurement per collar.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to demonstrate the issue by (1) checking every collar_id in data/input.csv for duplicates (all 24 are distinct), (2) searching workflow/analysis.py for any operation that could enter a unit more than once into the t-test, such as row duplication, merging, resampling, or per-subunit expansion (none exists, and a uniqueness guard would raise ValueError on any repeated collar_id), (3) checking whether repeated identical flux values in the restored group indicated the same measurement counted twice (they belong to different collars), and (4) recomputing group n, means, and the mean difference from the raw CSV to confirm the test statistics reflect exactly one entry per independent unit (they do: n=12 per group, means 6.00 and 18.00, difference 12.00). No path by which the same independent unit repeatedly enters the row-independent Welch procedure could be constructed from the supplied files.
